name: Washington Center for Equitable Growth — AI Workers & Competition RFP
description: Research grants studying how AI, automation, algorithmic management, and electronic surveillance affect US workers, wages, and market competition. Awards $25k–$80k over up to 2 years. Open to individual researchers and teams at think tanks, universities, and research institutions.
amount_notes: $25,000–$80,000; slightly larger grants possible if well-justified
notes: Most recent cycle closed Feb 2025; next RFP likely late 2026. Excellent thematic fit for think tank teams. Monitor equitablegrowth.org.

name: GitLab Foundation AI for Economic Opportunity Fund
description: Demonstration grants to US-based nonprofits using AI to measurably improve economic mobility for low-income populations. Each award is $250k plus OpenAI API credits and 6 months of technical support. The 2026 cohort (cycle 4) has already been announced; next cycle TBC.
amount_notes: $250,000 per org plus OpenAI API credits and cohort support
notes: 2026 cohort (16 orgs) announced March 5, 2026. Next open call TBC. Open to nonprofits, not think tanks directly unless nonprofit-registered.

name: Humanity AI — Pooled Philanthropic Fund (Labor & Economy Track)
organization: Humanity AI (Ford, MacArthur, Mellon, Omidyar, Mozilla, Packard, Kapor, Doris Duke, Lumina, Siegel Family Endowment)
description: A $500M, 5-year pooled fund from 10 leading foundations dedicated to people-centred AI development. The 'Labor & Economy' track focuses on equipping workers to thrive amid AI-driven transformation. Grants expected to flow in 2026; application details pending. Highest possible thematic alignment for think tank AI + future-of-work research.
amount_notes: $10M open call (part of the wider pooled fund)
notes: The open call is due 21 Oct 2026 and is limited to US-based nonprofits, so European organisations are not eligible. Focus areas are education, labour & economy, and the humanities, arts & culture.

name: Siegel Family Endowment — AI & Workforce Research Grants
description: Siegel Family Endowment investing $15.4M+ in grants focused on how workers shape AI's transformation of work. Supports research and programmes examining hiring, management, monitoring of workers, and evidence-based policies on worker data rights and AI impact. 2025–2026 cohort of Siegel Research Fellows announced.
amount_notes: $15.4M total announced; individual award amounts TBC
notes: Siegel is a Humanity AI coalition member with an active research fellowship programme. Explicitly focused on worker agency in AI transformation. Contact directly for 2026 grant deadlines.

name: OpenAI Foundation — AI for Humanity Grants
description: The OpenAI Foundation pledged $1 billion in grants over the next year to support AI for public benefit. Priorities include mitigating AI impacts on jobs, the economy, and mental health, as well as life science/health research. The first round (People-First AI Fund) awarded $40.5M to 208 US nonprofits; future open calls expected in 2026.
amount_notes: $1B total pledge; individual grant sizes vary ($50K–$500K in first round)
notes: First round closed Oct 2025. Foundation announced $1B commitment March 2026. Monitor openai.com/foundation for next open application cycle. Strong workforce/economic impact component.

name: Cooperative AI Foundation Research Grants
description: Research grants on AI cooperation, including understanding and evaluating cooperation-relevant capabilities. No fixed upper limit; cost-effectiveness is weighted. Priority areas include understanding AI cooperation propensities and multi-stakeholder AI governance relevant to labour and economic settings.
amount_notes: No fixed ceiling; applicants encouraged to be ambitious
notes: Rolling applications. Thematic overlap is indirect; strongest fit if research addresses cooperation in human-AI work systems.

name: Amazon Research Awards — Fairness in AI & Human-Computer Interaction
description: Unrestricted research gifts to academic institutions in areas including fairness in AI, knowledge management, NLP, and HCI. No IP rights retained by Amazon. Rolling calls; typically $50k–$150k per award. Relevant for think tanks affiliated with universities or structured as research institutions.
amount_notes: Typically $50,000–$150,000 unrestricted gift
notes: Requires institutional affiliation (university or nonprofit research org). Applications reviewed in rolling cycles; check portal for current open areas.

name: Google.org AI Opportunity Fund — US Workforce Development
description: Part of a $75M commitment to help over 1 million Americans learn AI skills through workforce development and education organisations. Focus on rural/under-served workers, public sector employees, small businesses, and nonprofits. Grants to best-in-class workforce orgs; not an open call but accepts relationship-based inquiries.
amount_notes: $75M total programme; individual grants vary; $15M sub-tranche for public sector recently announced
notes: Not an open RFP — Google.org selects partners proactively. Engage through introductions or foundation relations. Excellent fit for AI workforce research with practical outputs.

name: Knight Foundation — Ethics and Governance of AI Fund
description: Ongoing initiative supporting civil society organisations working on AI ethics, governance, and public interest. The Foundation has committed $7.6M to nine initial grantees; supports research on governance, norms, values, and responsible AI systems.
amount_notes: $7.6M committed across nine grantees; individual award sizes not published
notes: Rolling applications. Good fit for AI governance and policy research. Check knightfoundation.org for 2026 RFP details. May need to align with Knight's democracy and civics mission.

name: Schmidt Sciences — AI2050 Fellowship Programme
description: Supports exceptional researchers working on critical AI opportunities and hard problems including AI's impact on the economy and society. The 2025 cohort awarded $18M+ to 28 fellows. Co-chaired by Eric Schmidt and James Manyika.
amount_notes: $18M+ awarded to 28 fellows in 2025 cohort; individual amounts not disclosed
notes: Invitation and nomination only — no open application. Monitor for nomination windows and build a relationship with Schmidt Sciences programme staff.

name: Patrick J. McGovern Foundation — AI for Public Purpose
description: Annual grantmaking of ~$75M across 149 grants supporting AI and data solutions for public purpose, including digital literacy, workforce, crisis response, and climate resilience. Grants range from $100K to $1M+ and fund nonprofits, research institutions, and social enterprises globally.
amount_notes: $100K–$1M+; total annual spend ~$75M
notes: Proactive grantmaking model — foundation identifies and approaches partners, but unsolicited inquiries can be submitted via website. Workforce/labor is one of several focus areas alongside health equity, climate, journalism.

name: Middle Powers and Transformative AI — Request for Proposals
description: Around $10M for researchers, writers, builders and conveners working on how middle powers (e.g. European states, the UK, Canada, Japan, Korea) can stay relevant in the AI transition and help make it safe and broadly beneficial. Examples include policy research, crisis simulations and AI-policy journalism. Most grants are $100k–$2M. The initial application takes under an hour, and decisions are made on a rolling basis within about 8 weeks.
amount_notes: ~$10M total; most grants $100k–$2M
notes: Deadline Fri 23 Oct 2026, 23:59 PT. Individuals and organisations can apply. Astralis is a European funder with offices in Stockholm, London and Vienna. Reviews are rolling, so applying early helps. This is the strongest fit for European policy think tanks.

name: Project Tailwind — Call for Founders of Ambitious AI Safety Initiatives
description: Coefficient Giving's call for founders launching new organisations or initiatives that address catastrophic risks from AI, spanning technical safety, security, AI governance and policy, and fieldbuilding. Funding tiers are Pre-seed ($200k–$2M, no preliminary results needed), Seed ($2M–$20M) and Scale ($20M–$200M+).
amount_notes: Pre-seed $200k–$2M; Seed $2M–$20M; Scale $20M–$200M+
notes: Expression of interest due 2 Oct 2026. Non-US teams are eligible, and pre-seed applicants do not need a legal entity. It suits a new initiative or spin-out rather than core funding for an existing programme. Strong candidates may be fast-tracked to a pitch meeting.

name: AI for Science & Safety Nodes — Grants, Compute and Hub Space (Berlin / San Francisco)
description: Grants of $10k–$100k plus private compute and workspace at Foresight's AI Nodes in Berlin and San Francisco. Focus areas are AI for Security, Private AI, Decentralized & Cooperative AI, AI for Science & Epistemics, and AI for Neuro, Longevity and Nanotech. Outputs must be open source.
amount_notes: $10k–$100k per project (~$3M/yr); larger awards go to AI-safety areas; plus compute and hub access
notes: Deadline 31 Oct 2026, 23:59 PT; review takes about 3 months. Individuals, nonprofits and for-profits worldwide can apply. Applicants willing to work in person at a Node are strongly prioritised, and the Berlin node is convenient for European teams. Technical and tooling-heavy.

name: Transformative AI Fund (rolling)
description: Early-stage grants to individuals, new organisations, and existing organisations with new projects on transformative AI. Eligible work includes technical research, policy analysis, forecasting, advocacy, fieldbuilding, and neglected topics such as flourishing futures and digital sentience.
amount_notes: Typically $10k–$150k; rarely more than $300k
notes: Always open and fast. Good for pilots, a single research project, or bridge funding. European nonprofits are eligible.

name: Survival and Flourishing Fund — Rolling Application / Speculation Grants
description: A rolling application that requests an expedited Speculation Grant and also enters you into the next S-Process grant round. SFF is a major funder of AI safety and governance organisations. The 2026 round is estimated at $20–40M, with grants from $10k to $4M.
amount_notes: $10k–$4M (S-Process); Speculation Grants are smaller and faster
notes: You can apply even when no S-Process round is open. The 2026 main round closed 22 Apr 2026. Applying now positions you for the 2027 round. Check SFF's requirements for non-US charities or fiscal sponsorship.

name: Economic Futures Research Awards
description: Rapid grants for empirical, data-driven research on AI's economic impacts, including labour markets, productivity and distributional effects. The programme explicitly covers UK and EU researchers. Results are expected within about 6 months.
amount_notes: $10k–$50k plus $5k in Claude API credits
notes: Rolling. Well suited to data-heavy think-tank work such as econometrics, new data collection, or labour-market analysis. The grants are small but decisions are quick.

name: EIC Pathfinder Challenge 2026 — DeepRAP: Deep Reasoning, Abstraction & Planning
description: Funds fundamental advances in the reasoning, abstraction and planning of AI systems, with guarantees of explainability, safety and reliability. It is one of three 2026 Pathfinder Challenges, which share a €96M budget. Grants of up to about €4M cover 100% of eligible costs.
amount_notes: Up to ~€4M per project (≈$4.4M)
notes: Deadline 28 Oct 2026, 17:00 CEST. Nonprofit research organisations in EU and associated countries can apply. Check the call text for consortium rules. The work is technical and research-heavy, so it fits nonprofits with ML research capacity rather than policy shops.

name: Mercor AI Safety Fund Grants
description: $5M for frontier AI safety research by independent researchers, academics, PhD students and small teams. Topics include misalignment, sandbox escape, evaluation awareness, interpretability, oversight and control, and red-teaming. Funds can cover researcher time, API credits and conference travel.
amount_notes: $5M total pool; per-grant size not published
notes: Start with a focused expression of interest. The fund is aimed at small teams with well-scoped research that will be published. The official application page was not verified directly, so confirm the details via AISafety.com/funding.

name: Nuffield Foundation — Research, Development & Analysis Fund (Main Grants)
description: Two-stage call for research, development and analysis projects addressing the Foundation's priorities for improving social wellbeing in the UK. AI and data-driven projects are eligible where they address those priorities.
amount_notes: Up to £500k (≈$650k); up to £750k by prior agreement
notes: Outline application due 5 Oct 2026. Projects must aim to improve lives in the UK, so this suits UK-based think tanks only.

name: Digital Freedom Fund — Litigation & Pre-litigation Grants (AI & Digital Infrastructure Hub)
description: Grants for strategic litigation and pre-litigation research to advance digital rights in Europe, including through DFF's AI and Digital Infrastructure Strategic Litigation Hub on harms from AI and big-tech infrastructure.
amount_notes: Recent round: 13 grants worth €370k total
notes: The next call is expected to open in late Nov 2026 and close mid-Feb 2027 (exact dates TBC). Digital-rights NGOs, pro bono lawyers and litigators in Europe can apply. It suits AI-accountability and legal-research organisations.

name: Prototype Fund — Open-Source Public Interest Tech
organization: Open Knowledge Foundation Germany (funded by the German Federal Ministry of Research)
description: Funding for open-source software prototypes in the public interest, including civic tech, data tools and AI tooling.
amount_notes: Per-project amounts: see the current call text
notes: Due 30 Nov 2026. Open to individuals and small teams based in Germany, not established organisations. Useful for staff-led open data or AI tooling spin-offs. Individual eligibility rules and grant sizes were not verified directly.
